theater.name: Venezuela / Caribbean
theater.title: Venezuela and the Caribbean
theater.sub: The options the US has toward Venezuela and the Caribbean drug-boat campaign, and what followed the last times the US did something like each one.
theater.proxy_note: Every reply here is an act by Venezuela itself (its government, ministers or armed forces) or by an armed group. Venezuelan state media (Telesur, VTV) is used only as labelled claims of what the government says. Cuban, Russian and Trinidadian statements are not replies. After the Jan 3, 2026 capture of Maduro the interim government has cooperated with Washington; cooperative answers are not replies.
theater.hold_note: Hold cases are weeks, from Aug 11, 2025 on (the first Monday after the Maduro bounty was doubled), with no logged US sanction, deployment, boat strike, land strike, raid, seizure or talks move. Weeks inside the two stretches of near-daily boat strikes (Oct 27 - Nov 15, 2025 and Dec 15, 2025 - Jan 2, 2026) are left out, and so are weeks where outlet counts show boat strikes that the log does not hold one by one (Sep 22 - Oct 6 and Dec 1, 2025, and Jan 26 - Jun 22, 2026). Be careful: about 70 boat strikes are known and only 8 are logged one by one, so even the weeks that remain may have had an unlogged strike. The log is a sample, so a quiet week may only be a week where nothing was logged. Read option A as a rough sketch and do not compare it number for number with options that rest on well-reported cases.
theater.not_measured: Oil output and prices, migration, food and medicine supply, harm to ordinary Venezuelans from sanctions, and strain with Colombia, Cuba, Russia and Caribbean states are not measured. Only the five categories above are counted.
theater.under_logged: The log is a sample. Only 8 of about 70 boat strikes are logged one by one, 2020-2024 holds only a few key moves, and Venezuelan state media was not opened, so "none logged" is not proof nothing happened.
theater.small_n: Only 8 of about 70 boat strikes are logged one by one, most Venezuelan replies are statements (which do not count as an escalation reply here), and option G (raids or operations against leaders) has 1 case. Most options have only a handful of counted cases (the exact number is on each option), and options with fewer than 3 show "too few cases" instead of a percentage. Read every rate as a hint, not a forecast.
theater.us_hurt: Anyone killed or hurt in the US action

intensity.name: Tension level
intensity.note: Tension level counts logged hostile acts by Venezuela or an armed group (attacks, harassment of US assets, military mobilizations) in the 14 days before each date: 2 points each, +2 if someone died. Statements and economic steps are not counted. The log is a sample, so quiet stretches are understated.

people.name: Harm to people
people.other: Share of past cases where the logged source reports anyone killed or hurt in the US action itself or in a Venezuelan reply the log links to the move.
people.hold: Share of hold weeks in which a Venezuelan hostile act in the 7 days after hurt anyone.

rule.other: Counts when a logged source reports anyone killed or hurt in the US action itself (for example the people killed on a boat, as the source reports them; whether they were drug traffickers is not tested here) or in a Venezuelan reply the log links to the move. Linked replies are usually within 7 days; the longest logged lag is 18 days (#4031), so a case stays open for 18 days unless harm is already known.
rule.hold: Counts when a Venezuelan hostile act in the 7 days after the Monday hurt anyone.

escalation.name: Escalation
escalation.trigger: Share of past cases followed within 7 days by a hostile act from Venezuela or an armed group: an attack, harassment of US assets, or a military mobilization announced as a response. Words alone do not count.
escalation.other: Share of past cases followed within 7 days by any logged Venezuelan hostile act (an attack, harassment or a mobilization; timing only).
escalation.hold: Share of hold weeks followed within 7 days by a logged Venezuelan hostile act (an attack, harassment or a mobilization; timing only).

rule.trigger: Counts when Venezuela or an armed group took a hostile act within 7 days of the move: an attack, harassment of US assets, or a military mobilization announced as a response. A statement, a denunciation, a diplomatic step or an economic step does not count (a clear link or timing only, kept only when such an act is logged 0-7 days after the move). Several denunciations that the research file marks as weak replies are counted as no reply here.
rule.other: Counts when the log holds any Venezuelan hostile act (an attack, harassment or a mobilization) in the 7 days after the move (timing only, not shown to be a reply).

military.name: Military cost
military.reply: Share of past cases where the Venezuelan reply was armed action: an attack on, or armed harassment of, US forces or assets.
military.strike: Share of hold weeks with an armed Venezuelan attack or harassment of US assets in the 7 days after.
military.none: No direct military cost expected from the move itself, so this counts as 0%.

rule.reply: Counts when a Venezuelan reply the log links to the move was armed action (an attack on, or armed harassment of, US forces or assets; so far only military aircraft flying near USS Jason Dunham on Sep 4, 2025, #4019). A mobilization announcement, a militia call-up, a national exercise and a statement do not count.
rule.strike: Counts when an armed Venezuelan attack or harassment of US assets took place in the 7 days after the Monday.

economic.name: Economic harm
economic.other: Share of past cases followed within 14 days by a Venezuelan counter-measure: an oil or gas cut-off, an airline ban, or the expulsion of firms or diplomats (timing only, not shown to be caused by the US move).
economic.rule: Counts when Venezuela announced a counter-measure (an oil or gas cut-off, an airline ban, or the expulsion of firms or diplomats) within 14 days after the move. Only 3 are logged (#4002, #4029, #4041); #4041 is dated by the Reuters report, not the day it took effect. The window starts the day after the move, so a same-day act (the 2019 expulsion order, #4002) is not counted.

political.name: Political / diplomatic
political.other: Share of past cases NOT followed within 14 days by talks or a deal between the US and Venezuela (a call, a meeting, an oil deal or license, a prisoner swap, restored ties).  Statements and threats do not count.
political.rule: Counts when no US talks or deal with Venezuela (a call, a meeting, an oil deal or license, a prisoner swap, restored ties or an embassy reopening, directly or through a mediator) were logged within 14 days after the move. Statements, threats and appeals do not count as talks. Rule changed on 2026-10-26.

options.name: Talks or deals
options.what: Phone calls and talks, prisoner swaps, oil licenses and deals, and (after the capture) restored ties, an embassy and direct flights with the interim government.

cases.note: Saab-for-Americans swap, Dec 20, 2023. A deal; Maduro called it a 'triumph for truth' (AP). No hostile reply.

cases.title: Reuters, from four people briefed: call under 15 minutes; Maduro asks amnesty for himself and family, removal of sanctions on 100+ officials, and Delcy Rodriguez to lead an interim government; Trump rejects most and gives him a week to leave Venezuela. Deadline passed without Maduro leaving
cases.note: Trump-Maduro call, Nov 21, 2025. Maduro did not leave by the deadline; no hostile act found Nov 22-28. The next reply logged is to the FAA warning (4041).

cases.title: Trump says Venezuela will turn over 30 to 50 million barrels of sanctioned oil to be sold at market price, with revenue controlled 'by me'; asks Energy Secretary Wright to carry it out. Rodriguez answers 'My destiny is not determined by them, but by God' (AP via NPR)

Oil announcement, Jan 6, 2026 -> Rodriguez says her destiny is not set by the US (AP via NPR); the Jan 8 prisoner release (4054) followed. Words plus a concession.

cases.note: Ties restored, Mar 5, 2026. Rodriguez welcomed it on state TV (AP); a cooperative answer, not a reply.

cases.title: Al Jazeera: the US reopens its embassy in Caracas ('We are once again the US Embassy in Caracas'), nearly three months after the Maduro operation
cases.note: Embassy reopened, Mar 30, 2026. No hostile reply reported.

options.pros: No direct casualties, and none of the 8 counted talks and deals (#4006, #4007, #4035, #4052, #4057, #4058, #4060, #4063) was followed by a Venezuelan hostile act within 7 days. The 2026 deals and restored ties were with the interim government after the capture, which cooperated (#4052, #4057, #4058, #4060, #4063).

options.unknown: Only 8 counted cases, and 5 of them (2026 deals and ties) were with a cooperating interim government. Venezuela's own view of a deal reaches NAPOR only through statements reported by outlets.
